These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-thermostats-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 3 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Exact CSVR bath: conditional laws, fluctuations and kinetic correlation Implement the bath-only CSVR update for 1, 2 and 6 degrees of freedom; compare exact conditional moments/noncentral-chi-square laws, canonical Gamma fluctuations and kinetic correlations. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries kB=1, T=1.3, tau=0.5, h=0.2, 65536 independent replicas. Test three initial energies at each of three degree counts. No Hamiltonian force, positions, constraints or center-of-mass removal. Adopted numerical method Use the completed-square exact CIR transition with normal R and independent chi-square(Nf−1) S. The same R sets the sign of global alpha; S=0 for Nf=1. Reconstruct momentum from its unit direction and new radius without a tiny-K energy ratio. Reject K=0 because its direction is undefined. Correct K sampling does not thermalize momentum directions by global scaling alone. The bath-only exp(−t/tau) identity is not a full-MD kinetic ACF. CSVR versus Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations of two harmonic modes Compare global CSVR with local Langevin on two nondegenerate modes using the same OBABO splitting. Record position, momentum, temperature and total-energy distributions, fluctuations and correlations. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries m=kB=T=1, omega=(1,1.7), Nf=2. tau=0.25/1, h=0.1/0.05. Evolve 8192 canonically initialized replicas and a separate 4096-replica ensemble with q,p scaled by 1.4 to t=20. Correlation lags are 0/0.5/1/2/4. Adopted numerical method Both use exact O(h/2)–velocity-Verlet–O(h/2), or OBABO. CSVR applies one factor to all momenta; Langevin uses independent component-wise OU noise. gamma=1/(2 tau) matches bath-only K relaxation. The earlier BAOAB release is retained as a different splitting. Deterministic biases at h=0.2/0.1/0.05 establish second order. Check Langevin q,p,K,H correlations against independent discrete propagation; report CSVR correlations with independent-replica standard errors and tau/h dependence. Verification limits and failures Global-CSVR and local-Langevin dynamical correlations are not required to agree. CDF errors are maxima over five declared points, not whole-line KS distances. Canonical-start preservation and the heated-start finite-time check do not prove ergodicity; tests retain an invariant unexcited-axis counterexample.
